title: An illustrative compounding calculation
prompt: Implement all_correct(p,n)=p**n for independent successes. Validate 0<=p<=1 and integer n>=0. Example p=0.9,n=10 gives about 0.348678. This is not a match win-rate estimator.

title: Let actions change the next state
prompt: Implement rollout(policy,steps=8), starting threat=0,hp=5. Call policy(threat,hp) each step. wait adds 1 threat; defend subtracts 2 down to zero; reject other actions. Then threat>=3 costs one HP down to zero. Append (threat,hp) after each step and stop at zero HP. Example always waiting first yields (1,5),(2,5),(3,4).
tests:
a=rollout(lambda threat,hp:'wait',8)
assert a==[(1,5),(2,5),(3,4),(4,3),(5,2),(6,1),(7,0)], 'Apply damage after transition and stop at zero HP'
b=rollout(lambda threat,hp:'defend' if threat>=2 else 'wait',8)
assert len(b)==8 and all(hp==5 for threat,hp in b), 'A reactive policy should see updated threat and prevent damage'
assert rollout(lambda t,h:'wait',0)==[], 'Zero steps should produce no transitions'
hint: Keep state variables outside the loop and update them before recording.

title: Standardise the response mix
prompt: Implement standardised_rate(reference_mix,conditional_rates). Require identical category sets and mix shares summing to one (within 1e-9); all shares/rates must be in [0,1]. Return their weighted sum. Example mix {on_time:0.75,late:0.25}, rates {on_time:0.4,late:0.8} gives 0.5.
hint: Validate sets and ranges before summing mix[g]*rates[g].

title: Pair by scenario identity
prompt: Implement paired_gain(baseline,candidate), dictionaries mapping scenario IDs to binary known wins (0/1). Require identical nonempty ID sets and binary values; otherwise raise ValueError. Return mean candidate-minus-baseline. Example baseline {a:0,b:1}, candidate {b:1,a:1} gives 0.5 regardless of dictionary order.
hint: Once IDs match, use candidate[k]-baseline[k] for each baseline ID.
